narration.text: In summer, this field tilts toward the Sun's rays.
The oak tree stands in full leaf.
In winter, it tilts away, and the rays slant in.
The bare oak tree stands in snow.
In spring, it tilts neither way, and the oak tree buds.
Tilt, not distance, makes the seasons.

brief.title: Tilt, not distance, makes the seasons
brief.summary: Why summer and winter come from the tilt of the ground toward or away from the Sun, not from the distance to it, shown by one oak tree through a year.
